scope: Synthetic transport experiment isolating the placement of background completion notices. Both arms start with the same message structure and bounded pre-merge training source. Each arm/repetition has a distinct leading nonce to prevent cross-arm prefix warming. After each reply, control replaces its early second system message; candidate appends the same notice chronologically. The candidate retains prior notices as real conversations do; byte lengths therefore differ. Within-round order is randomized. This does not test coding quality or reproduce every runtime message. No reserved dataset is read.
primary: Post-initial cached/input fraction and token-priced input cost within six paired scenarios. Warmup reported separately, all failures retained; latency observational on a shared service. No production cache guarantee.
